title.title: The entropy photon-number inequality
title.subtitle: Claim: on a beam splitter, $N(\rho_C) \ge \eta N(\rho_A) + (1-\eta) N(\rho_B)$ for all finite-energy multimode inputs

beats.text: Two independent light beams mixed on a beam splitter of transmissivity $\eta$
Entropy photon number $N(\rho) = g^{-1}(S(\rho)/n)$ of the output, against $\eta$
Claim: the output always lands in the shaded region, on or above the line

achievement.label: Guha–Erkmen–Shapiro conjecture (2008)
achievement.context: Before: the weaker quantum entropy power inequality (2014) and Gaussian or thermal special cases
achievement.note: Gives the capacity region of the degraded pure-loss bosonic broadcast channel

verify.detail: The inequality for every $n \ge 1$ modes and finite-energy inputs; consequences are not
verify.ourCheck: We compared the Lean scope with the claim; we did not build it

sources.quote: The broadcast-capacity and minimum-output-entropy consequences are not formalized.

plain: Mix two light beams on a half-mirror: the output can't be more orderly than mixing plain thermal light

steps: Suppose two beams mixed to less entropy than thermal light
Compare them with thermal light at the same entropies
That forces a negative minimum, which the analysis rules out

data.smaller: a negative minimum of three entropies

voice.text: Two independent beams meet on a beam splitter. How much entropy must come out?
Suppose some pair beat thermal light; comparing with thermal references forces a contradiction.
Claimed: never less than thermal light.
